title: Tailoring magnetic and mechanical performance of 0.2 mm 3.3 wt% non-oriented silicon steel via controlled annealing parameters
abstract: Targeting efficient motors under China’s “dual carbon” policy, this study explores recrystallization annealing (900-960 °C/3.5 min) on 0.20 mm high-efficiency non-oriented electrical steel (HE-NOES) for new energy vehicle (NEV) traction motors.Hot rolling forms surface shear textures (Goss/Copper/Brass) and core α-fiber. Normalization enables complete recrystallization, producing 136 μm grains while suppressing γ-texture. Cold rolling develops the dominant γ-fiber and α-fiber. Increasing annealing temperature grows grains (87.2 μm to 120.4 μm), boosts λ-fiber, and reduces γ-fiber.Optimal 940 °C annealing achieves minimal core loss (P10/400 = 11.98 W/kg), high magnetic induction (B50 = 1.665 T), and yield strength (425 MPa), providing industrial guidance for ultra-thin silicon steel.
